summary.name: SLOs and SLIs: Best Practices for Modern, Complex Systems
summary.one_liner: A New Relic engineering blog post explaining how to define and measure service level indicators (SLIs) and service level objectives (SLOs) at system boundaries in a complex modern software platform.
use_cases: defining SLOs for a service platform
choosing which metrics to measure for availability
prioritizing reliability work for network and data tiers
creating a baseline for service levels in New Relic APM
summary.what_it_does: The post walks through how New Relic's reliability team defines SLIs and SLOs for a simplified version of its platform. It recommends focusing on system boundaries rather than individual components, and gives a recipe: identify boundaries, define plain-language availability, choose SLIs, measure a baseline, set SLOs, and iterate. It uses examples for ingest (HTTP 200 responses), message routing latency, database query response times at the 95th or 99th percentile, UI page load and JavaScript error rates, and network tier SLOs set higher than dependent services. It also describes a one-click baseline setup in New Relic APM's Service Levels report.
notable: Recommends setting SLIs at system boundaries instead of per component
Uses 95th or 99th percentile latency rather than averages
Describes one-click baseline SLO setup in New Relic APM Service Levels
Sets higher SLOs for hard dependencies such as the network tier
caveats: The one-click baseline setup and service level management are New Relic product features; the page mentions a free account signup but does not detail pricing
The post is a simplified, environment-specific example from New Relic's own architecture and may not apply directly to other systems
The page is a blog article rather than a standalone tool, and the author notes views are not New Relic's official support
